exact_document_excerpts.text:
Status: CONFIRMED shops and personal/shared improvements. IMPLEMENTED ambient guest shopping and fixed upgrade bundles. PROPOSED player retail checkout, inventory and free placement.

### Two different shopping systems

Astraea has 100 addressed storefronts. Guests browse, inspect, nominally purchase goods, carry parcels and return home. Stores staff receive bounded restock work. Current goods such as a wrapped keepsake or useful little gift are ambient metadata; they are not a stocked player catalog with prices and checkout. The player's actual purchases are the three fixed upgrade tracks.

Current repeated storefront names include Little Orbit, Thread House, Pocket Garden, The Parcel Room, Soft Landing, Moon Paper, Pebble and Reed, Tide Goods, Copper Buttons and Kind Curios. Unique R001 to R100 addresses prevent repeated brand names from becoming ambiguous destinations. These names are implementation content and remain open to final writing review.

### Retail architectural acceptance

The latest retail direction requires profiled curved architecture, recessed orange storefronts, monumental textured columns, integrated seating and planting, layered ceilings and convincing architectural light. Translate the supplied shopping-promenade reference into the project’s faux-pixelated early-2000s style with modern craft. Use editable custom assets or deterministic production meshes, with real enclosure, thresholds and integrated fixtures. Dressing an unchanged blockout is insufficient. Preserve gameplay, stable room IDs, capacity and usable routes. This is a design requirement, not acceptance of the current retail build.

## Facilities

The host supplies conservative, physically authored concurrent-use slots under `room.facility_slots`. Each slot has a stable ID, position and applicable activities, with optional family compatibility, authored approach, facing, duration and water loop. The model reserves one physical slot key across staff and guests. A browse/work position with combined activities therefore still admits only one owner.

Admission uses retained request order among currently eligible compatible waiters. Sleeping or eating people do not block an otherwise ready visitor. Reservations persist during travel and are rebuilt from the saved owners. Release, reuse, an interrupted visit and current save/import keep ownership unique. No capacity is inferred from room area.

The integrated registry includes sixteen dry changing cubicles, real shop/browse positions, separate water exercise cells and crew station/inspection places. Shopping remains at the reserved display instead of walking into another shopper's place. Swimmers use the reserved cell's loop and dry staging. A legacy swimmer without a slot leaves by the saved dry route before taking a new admitted visit.

Changing and shopping visits use their authored durations. Water visitors finish the actual water exit before releasing. Work defaults to a maximum 120-minute arrived station visit, training to eighteen minutes, and other authored facilities to forty-five minutes unless the host supplies a duration. Food and sleep take priority; overflow and turn-taking use quiet home rest and later retry.

Public amenity/social uses without a matching authored slot category retain their previous behavior. A room's work-only inspection places do not invent or restrict its public visitor capacity. Those remaining public activities are not yet bounded by this admission system. Crew work/training remains arrived time at an authored place, and breaks do not yet run the passenger paired-conversation system; specialist operations and crew conversation are separate future work.

## Evidence and limits

Godot 4.6.3, Compatibility renderer, metres, Y up; deck-local coordinates retain the active-deck origin. D09 is at +52.5 m; D10 at +61 m; usable height is 8.25 m. The current 640 × 360 SubViewport, CRT stage and native-resolution HUD remain the only rendering path. Player capsule diameter is 0.6 m; cart collider envelope is about 1.14 × 0.77 m. Automatic leaves now have independently verified closed/open transforms on all 18 decks.

D09_salon5 retains its ID, name, kind, centre (75,0,0), allocation X52..98/Z-34..34, front door (52,0,0), rear service door (98,0,0), and both operational sliding-door families. No accommodations, other registered destinations or room envelopes change. Social positions remain within the authored plan, with the existing centre-to-anchor approach kept free.

The terrace sample is the starboard garden-facing edge at Z-14..14. The entire tram strip X35..45 stays clear. The transverse route at Z0 stays clear and leads through the existing atrium portal at X48 to the room door at X52. The panoramic lift tower at (31.2,5) keeps its space and current decorative status. No floor holes are added.

## Current retail architectural acceptance

The 1 October retail direction requires profiled curved architecture, recessed orange shopfronts, monumental textured columns, integrated seating/planting, layered ceilings and convincing architectural lighting. Achieve the faux-pixelated early-2000s aesthetic through editable custom assets or deterministic production meshes, preserving room IDs, gameplay and clearance. Adding decoration to an unchanged blockout is insufficient. This is a production criterion, not current-build approval.

| 18 residential + six family commons + 12 habitat support rooms | Ordinary neighborhoods need sociable and quiet choices; family commons need shared garden clusters; habitat support needs useful adapted interfaces. Do not repeat the same coffee island in all 36 |
| Ten guest dining venues + one crew dining room | Guest rooms gather around a coherent service island/booth/ceiling composition with distinct mineral, damp, banquet and quiet profiles. Crew service is compact and practical. Existing seats and real approaches remain protected |
| 100 small stores + seven large shopping destinations | Keep every real allocation and address. Recessed entrances, angled browsing/display bays and fitted service edges vary by trade; do not move all stores to the atrium or create identical vending-door fronts |
| Grand atrium + 13 botanical rooms/terraces/walks | One botanical/water focal sequence, meaningful sheltered edges and useful open volume. Plants have canopy/shrub/groundcover hierarchy; the nursery is botanical |
